scores.evidence: Duplicate updates do no harm because applying a Yjs update twice has no extra effect.
scores.rationale: Claims about Yjs idempotence, CRDT convergence, Hocuspocus hooks, advisory locks, expand/contract migrations and fan-out math (50 editors ≈ 12k msg/s) are all accurate, with real limits stated honestly.

scores.evidence: Non-goals for v1: native mobile apps; full offline-first editing (short disconnects are handled); suggestion/track-changes mode
scores.rationale: Delivers exactly what real-time co-editing implies (sync, presence, undo, sharing, history), resolves ambiguities with stated defaults, and excludes scope explicitly with reasons; buildable by the assumed team.

scores.evidence: Kept separate so each table has one writer.
scores.rationale: Every component and table has a single named owner, data flows connect end to end, and choices (CRDT, token auth, single-writer tables) are honored consistently across all sections.

scores.evidence: deliberately dropping every 10th update makes it fail (proves the test can catch bugs)
scores.rationale: Spikes S1–S3 test the riskiest assumptions in week 1 before commitment, the convergence harness is mutation-checked, targets are labeled provisional, and a production canary continues validation after launch.

scores.evidence: Every assumption is marked [A] and collected in Section 5.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit with impact-if-wrong and validation timing, open questions carry defaults, and no invented specifics are presented as given facts.

scores.evidence: on a crash, unflushed updates (≤ 250 ms worth) are lost on the server. Clients reconnect with exponential backoff plus jitter
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures — crash mid-session, silent drift (canary), malicious viewer writes, revocation on live sockets, schema-corruption spread, duplicates, Postgres outage — each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Collab deploys: rolling, with drain (flush first, then close with "reconnect"). Rolling back is just another rolling deploy.
scores.rationale: Domain-meaningful signals (persisted lag, unsaved-age, canary mismatch), graceful drain, expand/contract migrations, runbooks and an on-call rotation sized to the 4-person team.

scores.evidence: about $800–1,500/month: 2× Collab and 2× API containers (2 vCPU / 4 GB), a mid-size managed Postgres
scores.rationale: Identifies the dominant drivers (Collab memory, DB IOPS), gives labeled range estimates, budget alerts, and quantifies the build-vs-buy trade-off (managed backend saves ~4–6 weeks).

scores.evidence: Hard: the stored format is Yjs binary
scores.rationale: Each decision carries an explicit reversibility rating and revisit trigger, the hardest one-way choices (persisted format, schema enablement point-of-no-return) are validated by week-1 spikes with scoped fallbacks.

scores.evidence: Redis is added in M3 so more than one Collab instance can run.
scores.rationale: Starts with two processes and one database, defers Redis, S3 and multi-instance until a stated need triggers them, while omitting nothing essential; deferred work has explicit triggers.

scores.evidence: Changes plan if forking is needed → custom server on y-protocols (+1.5–2 weeks)
scores.rationale: T0–T15 give concrete first steps with checkable done-when criteria, dependency-justified ordering, a per-engineer split, and explicit adaptation paths if spikes disappoint.
